newsitem.title: USA: Rifkin signs long-term deal with William Morris.
newsitem.headline: Rifkin signs long-term deal with William Morris.

text.p: William Morris Agency Friday said Arnold Rifkin has decided to remain with the agency, ending speculation he would take a top studio job at Sony Corp.'s Sony Pictures unit.
In a brief statement, William Morris said Rifkin, head of the agency's motion picture department, signed a "precedent-setting, long term agreement."
According to industry sources, Rifkin had been in talks with Sony about taking over as chairman of Sony's Columbia TriStar Pictures unit.
Sony has been looking for someone to replace current studio chief Mark Canton, who has come under fire for Sony's poor performance at the box office this summer.
According to published reports, Canton could be dismissed as early as today. Sony officials were not immediately available to comment on Canton's status or Rifkin's contract.
Rifkin's decision is a blow to Sony, which had hoped his contacts with the entertainment industry would provide a boost to the studio's reputation.
As head of the agency's motion picture unit, Rifkin has received praise for revitalising the department and signing a number of big-name stars to William Morris.
